w.sim.binaryStep: Compare the middle item at index {i}. Keep only the half that can contain the target.
w.sim.linearStep: Check index {i}. A linear scan may need to visit each item.
w.sim.nestedStep: Compare the pair at indexes {i} and {j}. Pairwise work grows about as n × n.
w.sim.branchStep: At depth {level}, the branching process has {n} possible states.
w.sim.branchStepOne: At depth {level}, the branching process has {n} possible state.
w.sim.treeEmpty: Press Next step to grow the recursion tree.

w.shapes.imageText: A small color image can be represented by height × width × color-channel values.
w.shapes.customerText: Each row is one customer; each column is a consistently ordered feature.
w.shapes.textText: An embedding is a dense vector that represents semantic information about text.
w.vector.aria: A vector on a two-dimensional coordinate plane
w.compose.explainBA: B acts first: [1,2] → {mid}, then A scales x: {mid} → {out}. Switch the order to see a different result.
w.compose.explainAB: A acts first: [1,2] → {mid}, then B shears x: {mid} → {out}. The order of matrix multiplication changes the result.
w.system.note: Least-squares fitting uses the same idea of finding parameters, but minimizes errors when no exact line fits every data point.
w.eigen.aria: Eigenvector direction before and after transformation
w.eigen.explanation: The vector [{v}] keeps its direction and is scaled by λ = {lambda}. The dashed arrow shows v; the solid arrow shows Av.
w.neuron.negative: The weighted sum is negative, so ReLU outputs zero.
w.neuron.positive: The weighted sum is positive, so ReLU passes it through.
study.videosHint: Free videos from other creators. Watch one after the lesson to see the idea explained a second way.
study.practiceHint: Solve these on LeetCode (free account). Start with the easy ones.
w.ram.readout: address(nums[{i}]) = {base} + {i} × {b} = {addr}  →  value {v}. One multiplication and one addition, no matter how long the array is: O(1).
w.sarr.initial: Try inserting in the middle and watch the orange cells shift.
w.sarr.pushed: Wrote to the next free slot: O(1).
w.sarr.inserted: Shifted {k} element(s) right to make room: O(n).
w.sarr.removed: Shifted {k} element(s) left to close the gap: O(n).
w.sarr.full: The array is full. A static array cannot grow.
w.darr.initial: Push values and watch the capacity double when the array is full.
w.darr.resized: Full! Allocated a new array of capacity {cap} and copied {n} element(s). Rare, so the average stays O(1).
w.darr.limit: That is enough for this demo. Press Reset.
w.stack.initial: Last in, first out: you can only touch the top.
w.queue.initial: First in, first out: join at the back, leave from the front.
w.queue.dequeued: {v} left from the front: O(1) with a linked list or deque.
w.list.head: head
w.list.initial: Each node points to the next one. Try searching: you must walk from the head.
w.list.initialDoubly: Each node points both ways, so you can remove from either end in O(1).
w.list.addedHead: New node {v} now points to the old head: O(1).
w.list.addedTail: Old tail now points to {v}: O(1) because we keep a tail pointer.
w.list.addedTailDoubly: Linked {v} after the tail in both directions: O(1).
w.list.removedHead: Removed {v}: head moves to the next node, O(1).
w.list.removedTail: Removed {v}: tail moves back using prev, O(1).
w.list.notFound: {v} is not in the list. Visited all {k} node(s): O(n).
w.fact.initial: Press Next step to call factorial(n) and watch frames stack up.
w.fact.call: factorial({k}) needs factorial({k1}) first, so a new frame is pushed.
w.fact.base: factorial(1) hits the base case and returns 1 without calling again.
w.fact.returnBase: Base case returns 1. Now the frames unwind.
w.fact.ret: factorial({k}) returns {k} × {prev} = {r} and its frame is popped.
w.fact.done: Done: factorial({n}) = {r}. Each call used one frame: O(n) time and O(n) stack space.
w.fib.memoOff: {calls} calls. Notice the same subproblems (like fib(2)) computed again and again: about O(2ⁿ).
w.fib.memoOn: {calls} calls instead of {naive}. Orange dashed nodes reuse a saved answer: O(n).
w.sort.initial: Press Next step or Play to start sorting.
w.sort.insPick: Take {v} and slide it left into the sorted part (green).
w.sort.mergeSplit: Split indexes {lo}–{hi} into two halves at {mid}.
w.sort.mergeJoin: Merge the two sorted halves of {lo}–{hi} by repeatedly taking the smaller front item.
w.sort.quickPivot: Pivot = {v} (orange). Move everything smaller to its left.
w.sort.quickSmall: {v} is smaller than the pivot: swap it into the left side.
w.sort.quickPlace: Pivot {v} lands at index {i}, its final position. Recurse on each side.
w.sort.bucketCount: Drop {v} into bucket {v}: no comparisons needed.
w.bsearch.initial: L and R mark the range that can still contain the target. Press Next step.
w.bsearch.goRight: {v} < {t}: the target must be to the right. Move L past M.
w.bsearch.goLeft: {v} > {t}: the target must be to the left. Move R before M.
w.bsearch.missing: L passed R: {t} is not in the array ({n} checks).
w.guess.initial: Pick a secret number. The computer guesses the middle of the remaining range each time.
w.guess.initialRange: Range 1–{max}: binary search needs at most {worst} guesses.
w.guess.done: Found it in {n} guesses. Guessing 1, 2, 3, … would have taken {linear}.
w.tree.initial: Click any node to see its depth, height, and children.
w.tree.rootMsg: The root is the only node without a parent.
w.tree.leavesMsg: Leaves are nodes with no children.
w.tree.heightMsg: The longest root-to-leaf path has {h} levels: that is the tree height.
w.tree.full: That is enough nodes for this demo. Press ↺.
w.bst.initial: Every left subtree is smaller and every right subtree is bigger. Search for a value.
w.bst.goLeft: {t} < {v}: go left, skipping the whole right subtree.
w.bst.goRight: {t} > {v}: go right, skipping the whole left subtree.
w.bst.missing: Hit an empty child: {t} is not in the tree ({n} nodes visited).
w.bstedit.aria: A binary search tree you can edit
w.bstedit.initial: Insert or remove values. Try removing 3 (two children) and 1 (a leaf).
w.bstedit.inserted: Inserted {v} as a new leaf after {n} comparison(s).
w.bstedit.exists: {v} is already in the tree; a set keeps one copy.
w.bstedit.leaf: Case 1: {v} was a leaf, so it was simply cut off.
w.bstedit.one: Case 2: {v} had one child, which took its place.
w.bstedit.two: Case 3: {v} had two children. Its in-order successor {s} (smallest on the right) replaced it.
w.bstedit.full: Tree full for this demo. Press ↺.
w.dfs.initial: Pick an order and step through it.
w.dfs.preRule: visit a node before its children
w.dfs.inRule: finish the left subtree, visit the node, then the right subtree
w.dfs.postRule: visit a node only after both children
w.dfs.done: Done: {out}. Every node visited once: O(n).
w.bfs.initial: BFS visits the tree level by level using a queue. Orange nodes are waiting in the queue.
w.bfs.newLevel: Start level {l}: dequeue {v} and enqueue its children.
w.bfs.done: Queue empty: every node visited once, level by level. O(n).
w.bstmap.aria: A sorted map stored as a binary search tree
w.bstmap.initial: Keys are compared alphabetically, so the map always iterates in sorted order.
w.bstmap.added: Added {k}={v} after {n} step(s) down the tree.
w.bstmap.updated: {k} already existed, so its value was updated to {v}.
w.bstmap.missing: {k} is not a key in the map ({n} steps).
w.bstmap.full: Map full for this demo. Press ↺.
w.maze.aria: A tree maze: find a root-to-leaf path that avoids walls
w.maze.initial: ■ nodes are walls. Find any path from the root to a leaf without touching a wall.
w.maze.choose: Choose {v}: add it to the path and explore its children.
w.maze.backtrack: Dead end below {v}: remove it from the path and go back (backtrack).
w.maze.noPath: Every branch is blocked: no valid path exists.
catalog.bookmarksEmpty: No bookmarks yet. Use the ☆ Bookmark button on any lesson to save it here.
code.loadingPython: Loading Python… (first run downloads about 10 MB, then it is cached)
code.timeout: Stopped after {s} s. Is there an infinite loop?
code.differs: Output differs from the expected result
code.cppNote: C++ cannot run in the browser, so this is the output of a real clang++ (C++17) run. Switch to Python or JavaScript to edit and run.
code.resetDone: Code restored to the original example
catalog.reorderHint: Drag the cards or use ← → to change the order. It is saved on this device and used in the sidebar too.
w.heap.aria: A heap drawn as a tree and as an array
w.heap.initial: Click any node or array cell to see its parent and children.
w.heap.rootMin: The root {v} is the smallest value. Every parent is ≤ its children.
w.heap.rootMax: The root {v} is the largest value. Every parent is ≥ its children.
w.heap.broken: Not a heap: index {i} ({v}) is on the wrong side of its parent ({p}). Red nodes break the rule.
w.heappp.aria: A min-heap that animates push and pop
w.heappp.initial: Push a value to watch it sift up, or pop to watch the root be replaced and sift down.
w.heappp.added: Put {v} at the end of the array (index {i}).
w.heappp.pushDone: {v} is in place after {n} swap(s): O(log n).
w.heappp.takeRoot: The root {v} is the minimum. Take it.
w.heappp.lastToRoot: Move the last item {v} to the root.
w.heappp.popDone: Popped {v}. The heap was repaired with {n} swap(s): O(log n).
w.heappp.full: Heap full for this demo. Press ↺.
w.heapify.aria: Building a heap from an array
w.heapify.initial: An unordered array. Heapify fixes it from the last parent back to the root.
w.heapify.siftStart: Sift down index {i} (value {v}). Its subtrees are already heaps.
w.heapify.swap: Swap with the smaller child: {c} goes up, {v} goes down.
w.heapify.done: Done: a valid min-heap after {n} swap(s). Heapify is O(n), faster than n pushes.
w.hashcount.sample: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog and the dog sleeps
w.hashcount.summary: {n} words, {u} unique keys, built in one pass.
w.hashcount.missing: "{w}" is not a key: checked in O(1).
w.buckets.initial: Each key is hashed to a bucket. Add keys until the load factor passes 0.75.
w.buckets.collision: Collision! The bucket now chains {n} keys.
w.buckets.resized: Load factor > 0.75, so the table doubled to {n} buckets and every key was rehashed.
w.buckets.found: Found "{k}" at position {c} in the chain.
w.buckets.full: Table full for this demo. Press ↺.
w.graphrep.aria: A small graph and its representations
w.graphrep.initial: Click matrix cells to add or remove edges; click a node to see its neighbours.
w.graphrep.added: Added edge {a}–{b} (both matrix cells change in an undirected graph).
w.graphrep.directedOn: Directed: an edge A→B no longer means B→A, so the matrix can be asymmetric.
w.graphrep.directedOff: Undirected: every edge works both ways, so the matrix is symmetric.
w.grid.initialDfs: Click cells to add or remove walls. DFS explores one path at a time and backtracks.
w.grid.initialBfs: Click cells to add or remove walls. BFS spreads out one layer at a time; numbers are distances.
w.grid.dfsFound: Reached the goal! Path #{n} uses {len} moves. Backtracking to look for more.
w.grid.dfsDone: Search finished: {n} different path(s) from S to G.
w.grid.bfsLayer: Layer {d}: {n} cell(s) are exactly {d} steps from the start.
w.grid.bfsDone: Goal reached at distance {d}. The green cells are a shortest path.
w.grid.unreachable: The goal cannot be reached: walls block every route.
w.graphbfs.aria: A directed graph explored with breadth-first search
w.graphbfs.initial: Edit edges with From/To, pick a start node, then step through BFS. The number on a node is its distance.
w.graphbfs.visit: Visit {n} (distance {d}) and enqueue its new neighbours: {list}.
w.graphbfs.visitNone: Visit {n} (distance {d}); it has no new neighbours.
w.graphbfs.doneAll: Done: every node is reachable. Time O(V + E).
w.graphbfs.doneSome: Done. Not reachable from the start: {list}.
w.dp1.initial: dp[0] = dp[1] = 1. Each new cell is the sum of the two before it.
w.dp1.done: dp[{n}] = {v} ways, in {steps} additions. Plain recursion would make {naive} calls.
w.dp2.initial: Click cells to toggle obstacles. Then fill the table row by row: paths = from above + from the left.
w.dp2.start: Start cell: exactly 1 way to be here.
w.dp2.done: {v} unique path(s), computed by visiting each of the {cells} cells once: O(rows × cols).
w.bits.initial: Click the bits of a and b to flip them.
w.bits.and: AND keeps a 1 only where both a ({a}) and b ({b}) have 1 → {r}.
w.bits.or: OR gives 1 where a ({a}) or b ({b}) has a 1 → {r}.
w.bits.xor: XOR gives 1 where a ({a}) and b ({b}) differ → {r}. x ^ x = 0.
w.bits.shl: Shift left by 1 doubles a: {a} × 2 = {r} (kept to 8 bits).
w.bits.shr: Shift right by 1 halves a, dropping the remainder: {a} // 2 = {r}.
w.bits.not: NOT flips every bit of a ({a}) → {r} (8-bit).
w.lru.initial: Get and put keys. The map finds a node in O(1); the list moves it to the recent end in O(1).
w.lru.hit: Hit: key {k} found and moved to the most-recent end.
w.lru.inserted: Inserted key {k} at the most-recent end.
w.lru.updated: Updated key {k} and marked it most recent.
w.lru.evict: Over capacity {c}: evicted the least recently used key {k}.
sync.title: Sync across devices
sync.lead: Keep completed lessons, bookmarks, notes, edited code and course order in step on every device, using a private file in your own GitHub account.
sync.step1Text: Tick only the "gist" permission (the link pre-selects it), choose an expiry, then generate and copy the token.
sync.step2Title: Paste it here on each device
sync.connected: Connected as @{login}. Your progress is synced.
sync.privacy: The token is stored only in this browser and can only read and write gists. Your data goes to a secret gist: it is not listed anywhere, but anyone with its exact link could read it, so keep private thoughts out of reflections. Theme and language stay per device.
sync.confirmDisconnect: Stop syncing on this device? Your progress stays here and in the gist; only the token is removed from this browser.
sync.whatSyncs: Syncs automatically when a page opens, when you return to the tab, and a few seconds after each change.
sync.errToken: GitHub rejected this token. Check that it was copied completely and has the "gist" permission.
sync.errAuth: The token no longer works (expired or revoked). Disconnect, then connect with a new token.
sync.errGeneric: Could not sync ({e}). Your progress is safe on this device; it will retry automatically.
sync.state_auth: Sync token expired: open to reconnect
lesson.completeHint: Click again to mark the lesson as not done
